boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain CUNY Bernard M Baruch College
boards.description: Build an under-21-safe late-night ritual board. Every card needs a currently verifiable destination, a direct source supporting late availability, and a conservative explanation of why it matters near this campus. Do not invent student habits, signature orders, popularity, or current hours. Bars and 21+-only venues are prohibited.

cards.title: Late Study at Newman Library
cards.subtitle: 151 East 25th Street
cards.notes: Utilize the library's extended hours during the academic semester for late-night research and group study sessions.
cards.short_summary: The primary academic hub for Baruch students, offering late-night study hours and technology loans.
cards.evidence_claim: The Newman Library is open until 11:00 PM on weekdays during the academic semester.
cards.source_title: Hours - Newman Library | Baruch College - CUNY
cards.access_notes: Open until 11:00 PM Monday through Thursday during the fall and spring semesters.

cards.title: Warm Cookies on 25th Street
cards.subtitle: 237 East 25th Street
cards.notes: Stop by for warm cookies and ice cream sandwiches just steps from the Newman Vertical Campus.
cards.short_summary: A popular late-night bakery specializing in warm cookies delivered or served in-store until the early morning.
cards.evidence_claim: The 25th Street location serves warm cookies until 1:00 AM or later most nights.
cards.source_title: Insomnia Cookies | Warm Cookie Delivery & Baked Treats Until Late Night
cards.access_notes: Open until 1:00 AM Sunday-Wednesday and 3:00 AM Thursday-Saturday.

cards.title: 24/7 Convenience on 23rd
cards.subtitle: 107 East 23rd Street
cards.notes: Grab quick snacks, beverages, or basic supplies at any hour from this corner convenience store.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour convenience store located directly across from the Baruch College campus buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: The 7-Eleven at 107 East 23rd Street is open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
cards.source_title: 107 E 23rd St New York NY 10010 - 7-Eleven
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 for snacks and essentials.

cards.title: Signature Slices on 14th
cards.subtitle: 321 East 14th Street
cards.notes: Try the famous artichoke slice or a classic Margherita at this late-night East Village staple.
cards.short_summary: A well-known pizza shop famous for its thick, creamy artichoke slices and late-night service.
cards.evidence_claim: The East Village location is open daily from 11:00 AM to 5:00 AM.
cards.source_title: East Village | Hours + Location - Artichoke Basille's Pizza
cards.access_notes: Open until 5:00 AM daily for walk-up service.

cards.title: Weekend Pierogies at Veselka
cards.subtitle: 144 2nd Avenue
cards.notes: Enjoy traditional Ukrainian pierogies and borscht during the restaurant's weekend 24-hour service.
cards.short_summary: A historic Ukrainian diner in the East Village that recently restored 24-hour service on weekends.
cards.evidence_claim: Veselka is open 24 hours on Fridays and Saturdays.
cards.source_title: Our Locations - Veselka
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours on Friday and Saturday; closes at midnight on other nights.

cards.title: Platters on 14th Street
cards.subtitle: 307 East 14th Street
cards.notes: Order a classic chicken and gyro platter with white sauce at this brick-and-mortar location.
cards.short_summary: A permanent storefront of the famous NYC halal cart, serving platters and sandwiches late into the night.
cards.evidence_claim: The 14th Street location is open until 4:00 AM daily.
cards.source_title: New York - 307 E 14 St. | The Halal Guys
cards.access_notes: Open until 4:00 AM daily for dine-in and takeout.

cards.title: Falafel on St. Marks
cards.subtitle: 30 St. Marks Place
cards.notes: Grab an affordable falafel sandwich or shawarma platter at this iconic East Village spot.
cards.short_summary: One of the oldest falafel restaurants in the city, providing quick and inexpensive Middle Eastern fare.
cards.evidence_claim: The St. Marks Place location is open until 11:00 PM daily.
cards.source_title: East Village, NYC | Hours + Location | Mamoun's Falafel
cards.access_notes: Open until 11:00 PM daily for takeout and delivery.

cards.title: Classic Slices on 14th
cards.subtitle: 150 East 14th Street
cards.notes: Experience a quintessential New York slice at this reliable late-night outpost near Union Square.
cards.short_summary: A branch of the legendary Greenwich Village pizzeria, known for its consistent, high-quality NYC slices.
cards.evidence_claim: The 14th Street location is open until 4:00 AM or later daily.
cards.source_title: Locations — Joe's Pizza
cards.access_notes: Open until 4:00 AM daily for walk-up slices.

cards.title: 24-Hour Diner Fare
cards.subtitle: 481 8th Avenue
cards.notes: Head to this classic 24-hour diner for breakfast at any hour or late-night comfort food like disco fries.
cards.short_summary: A large, iconic American diner in Midtown Manhattan that never closes.
cards.evidence_claim: Tick Tock Diner is open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
cards.source_title: Contact - Tick Tock Diner NY
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 for full-service dining.

cards.title: Late Night Deli Classics
cards.subtitle: 548 3rd Avenue
cards.notes: Visit this traditional Jewish deli for massive pastrami sandwiches and matzo ball soup until late evening.
cards.short_summary: A classic NYC deli known for its extensive menu and generous portions, located a short walk from campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Sarge's is open daily until 10:00 PM for indoor dining.
cards.source_title: Sarge's Delicatessen & Diner
cards.access_notes: Open 10:00 AM to 10:00 PM daily.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the essential student-utilized spaces across Baruch's urban campus, from quiet library zones to modern student centers and outdoor plazas.

cards.entity_name: Allen G. and Mary E. Aaronson Student Center
cards.title: The Aaronson Student Center
cards.subtitle: Undergraduate Lounge in the Historic Post Office
cards.notes: Enter on East 24th Street to access this 5,500-square-foot lounge featuring high ceilings and colorful furniture for socializing and studying.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated undergraduate student center located within the historic Madison Square Post Office building.
cards.evidence_claim: The Aaronson Student Center is located in the back of the Madison Square Post Office with an entrance on East 24th Street and is open for undergraduate students.
cards.source_title: Student Center Spaces - Student Affairs | Baruch College
cards.access_notes: Open Monday–Thursday 9:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m. and Friday until 5:00 p.m. during Fall/Spring semesters.

cards.title: Clivner=Field Plaza
cards.subtitle: The Campus's Outdoor Living Room
cards.notes: Gather on East 25th Street between Lexington and Third Avenues for outdoor seating, community events, and a break from the city's pace.
cards.short_summary: A permanent pedestrian plaza on East 25th Street serving as the geographic and social center of the Baruch campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Clivner=Field Pedestrian Plaza is located along East 25th Street between Lexington and Third avenues and serves as a gathering space for students.
cards.source_title: Baruch College Celebrates Official Opening of Clivner=Field Plaza - News Center
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible outdoor pedestrian plaza.

cards.title: Newman Library Low Noise Zone
cards.subtitle: Focused Study on the Third Floor
cards.notes: Head to the 3rd floor for a designated low-noise environment equipped with desktop computers and individual study carrels.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated low-noise study floor within the William and Anita Newman Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The 3rd floor of the Newman Library is designated as a Low Noise Zone and includes desktop computers and study carrels.
cards.source_title: Floor Plans - Newman Library | Baruch College - CUNY
cards.access_notes: Access requires a valid Baruch ID; hours vary by semester.

cards.title: NVC Main Cafeteria
cards.subtitle: Central Hub for Dining and Study
cards.notes: Visit the first floor of the NVC for the main dining area, which doubles as a high-capacity study space during off-peak hours.
cards.short_summary: The primary dining and large-scale gathering space located on the ground floor of the Newman Vertical Campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Newman Vertical Campus 1st Floor Cafeteria is listed as a primary place to study on campus with extensive weekday hours.
cards.source_title: Places To Study on Campus - Student Affairs | Baruch College
cards.access_notes: Open Monday–Friday 7:30 a.m.–10:00 p.m. and weekends 7:30 a.m.–5:00 p.m.

cards.title: 17 Lex MPR
cards.subtitle: Quiet Lounge in the Field Building
cards.notes: Find this first-floor lounge at 17 Lexington Avenue for a quiet spot with couches and tables, ideal for both undergrads and grads.
cards.short_summary: A versatile student lounge and study area located on the first floor of the Lawrence and Eris Field Building.
cards.evidence_claim: The 17 Lex Multi-Purpose Room (MPR) is located on the 1st floor of 17 Lexington Avenue and is open for all students.
cards.source_title: Student Center Spaces - Student Affairs | Baruch College
cards.access_notes: Open Monday–Thursday 9:30 a.m.–7:30 p.m. and Friday until 4:30 p.m. during semesters.

cards.title: Library Whisper Zones
cards.subtitle: Silent Study on Floors 4 and 5
cards.notes: Utilize the 4th and 5th floors for absolute silence; these floors are strictly designated for individual, quiet work.
cards.short_summary: The highest levels of the Newman Library dedicated to silent, individual study.
cards.evidence_claim: The 4th and 5th floors of the Newman Library are designated as Whisper Zones for silent study.
cards.source_title: Floor Plans - Newman Library | Baruch College - CUNY
cards.access_notes: Access requires a valid Baruch ID; 5th floor includes carrels for graduate students.

cards.title: NVC Elevator Bank Lounges
cards.subtitle: Quick Stops Between Classes
cards.notes: Look for open study areas located near the elevator banks on various floors of the Newman Vertical Campus for quick study sessions.
cards.short_summary: Informal study lounges distributed throughout the upper floors of the Newman Vertical Campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Open study areas are located on various floors near elevator banks in the Newman Vertical Campus.
cards.source_title: Places To Study on Campus - Student Affairs | Baruch College
cards.access_notes: Available during building hours, typically 7:30 a.m.–10:00 p.m. on weekdays.

cards.title: The MakerHub
cards.subtitle: Innovation and Prototyping Space
cards.notes: Access 3D printers, robotics, and circuit technology at the Field Center to bring entrepreneurial projects to life.
cards.short_summary: A creative technology space within the Lawrence N. Field Center for Entrepreneurship.
cards.evidence_claim: The Field Center for Entrepreneurship offers access to robotics, 3D printers, and more through its MakerHub.
cards.source_title: Lawrence N. Field Center for Entrepreneurship - Zicklin School of Business
cards.access_notes: Located in the Newman Vertical Campus; check center for specific MakerHub hours.

cards.title: Wasserman Trading Floor
cards.subtitle: Real-Time Financial Learning
cards.notes: Experience a professional trading environment with Bloomberg terminals and real-time data feeds in the Subotnick Financial Services Center.
cards.short_summary: A high-tech financial simulation lab located in the Information and Technology Building.
cards.evidence_claim: The Subotnick Financial Services Center provides experiential learning through its Wasserman Trading Floor at 151 East 25th Street.
cards.source_title: Subotnick Financial Services Center - Zicklin School of Business
cards.access_notes: Located in the Information and Technology Building; access typically for students in related courses.

cards.title: Mason Hall
cards.subtitle: Historic Performance Venue
cards.notes: Attend major campus events and performances in this landmark 1,100-seat auditorium located within the 17 Lex building.
cards.short_summary: The primary large-scale auditorium and performance space for Baruch College, located in the historic Field Building.
cards.evidence_claim: Mason Hall is an auditorium-style venue located on the main floor of the landmark 17 Lexington Avenue building.
cards.source_title: Mason Hall - Baruch Performing Arts Center
cards.access_notes: Entrance on 23rd Street; public events subject to reopening schedule.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Explore free social spaces and activities at Baruch College, from public pedestrian plazas and art galleries to student-only fitness centers and lounges.

cards.title: Lounge at Clivner=Field Plaza
cards.subtitle: East 25th Street between Lexington and 3rd Avenues
cards.notes: Relax at this permanent pedestrian plaza featuring seating and greenery. It serves as the geographic center of campus for students and the local community.
cards.short_summary: A public pedestrian plaza on East 25th Street providing open-air seating and a central gathering spot for the Baruch community.
cards.evidence_claim: The Clivner=Field Pedestrian Plaza is a permanent public space located along East 25th Street that is free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: About the Clivner=Field Plaza - Baruch College
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 to the public; no ID required for the outdoor plaza area.

cards.title: Visit the Mishkin Gallery
cards.subtitle: 135 East 22nd Street
cards.notes: View museum-quality contemporary art exhibitions at this campus gallery. All programs and exhibitions are free and open to the general public.
cards.short_summary: A campus art gallery presenting five exhibitions annually that are free and open to the public.
cards.evidence_claim: All Mishkin Gallery programs are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Mishkin Gallery - Baruch College
cards.access_notes: Open Monday to Friday, 11:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. during exhibitions.

cards.title: Work Out at the ARC
cards.subtitle: Newman Vertical Campus, Basement Levels
cards.notes: Access the fitness center, swimming pool, and racquetball courts for free. You must present a valid Baruch student ID for entry.
cards.short_summary: A multi-level fitness facility available for free to all currently enrolled Baruch students.
cards.evidence_claim: All enrolled Baruch College undergraduate and graduate students are granted free access to the ARC with a valid student ID card.
cards.source_title: Membership Information - Baruch College Athletics
cards.access_notes: Requires valid Baruch student ID; hours vary by facility (gym, pool, fitness center).

cards.title: Hang at Aaronson Student Center
cards.subtitle: Newman Vertical Campus
cards.notes: Meet friends or study in this dedicated undergraduate lounge. It features comfortable seating and is open late on weekdays during the semester.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated social and study space for undergraduate students located within the Newman Vertical Campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Aaronson Student Center (ASC) is open for all undergraduate students and is free to use.
cards.source_title: Student Center Spaces - Baruch College
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Thursday until 8:00 p.m. and Friday until 5:00 p.m. during the semester.

cards.title: Study at Newman Library
cards.subtitle: 151 East 25th Street
cards.notes: Utilize multiple floors of quiet study zones and collaborative spaces. Access is free for students with a valid CUNY ID card.
cards.short_summary: The primary campus library offering extensive study areas and research resources for students.
cards.evidence_claim: The library provides study areas and is accessible to Baruch students with a valid ID.
cards.source_title: Library Access Policy - Newman Library
cards.access_notes: Valid Baruch or CUNY ID required for entry; check library site for current floor-specific hours.

cards.title: Attend a Free Concert
cards.subtitle: Baruch Performing Arts Center
cards.notes: Enjoy professional musical performances throughout the semester. These concerts are free and open to the Baruch community and the public.
cards.short_summary: A series of free musical performances hosted by the Department of Fine and Performing Arts.
cards.evidence_claim: The Aaron Silberman Concert Series offers free concerts made possible through a gift to the Baruch College Fund.
cards.source_title: Aaron Silberman Concert Series - Baruch College
cards.access_notes: Events are scheduled periodically; check the BPAC calendar for specific dates and times.

cards.title: Picnic at Madison Square Park
cards.subtitle: 11 Madison Avenue
cards.notes: Walk one block west of campus to this historic park. It offers free art installations, seasonal events, and plenty of lawn space for lunch.
cards.short_summary: A nearby public park frequently used by Baruch students for outdoor breaks and social gatherings.
cards.evidence_claim: Madison Square Park is a public park with free programs, including contemporary art installations and concerts.
cards.source_title: Events - Madison Square Park - NYC Parks
cards.access_notes: Public park open daily from 6:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m.

cards.title: Join a Club Meeting
cards.subtitle: Newman Vertical Campus
cards.notes: Participate in student organizations during the dedicated Thursday break. Most undergraduate clubs meet between 12:40 p.m. and 2:20 p.m.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated time block every Thursday for student clubs to meet and host free activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Most undergraduate clubs meet on Thursdays, 12:40 to 2:20 pm (Club Hours).
cards.source_title: Student Clubs and Organizations - Baruch College
cards.access_notes: Primarily for Baruch students; meetings occur in various rooms throughout the NVC.

cards.title: Celebrate Welcome Week
cards.subtitle: Campus-wide
cards.notes: Kick off the semester with free social events, food, and music. These activities are hosted by Student Government and the Office of Student Life.
cards.short_summary: A series of free social events held at the start of the Fall and Spring semesters to welcome students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Office of Student Life hosts Welcome Week events at the beginning of the Fall and Spring semesters.
cards.source_title: Special Events and Programs - Baruch College
cards.access_notes: Occurs in August and January; open to all Baruch students.

cards.title: Relax at 17 Lex Lounge
cards.subtitle: Lawrence and Eris Field Building
cards.notes: Visit the newly renovated lounge on the first floor for social interaction and charging stations. It is designed for both study and relaxation.
cards.short_summary: A versatile student space on the first floor of the historic Field Building.
cards.evidence_claim: A new student lounge at 17 Lex on the first floor is designed for collaboration, relaxation, and engagement.
cards.source_title: An Update on Campus Projects - Baruch College
cards.access_notes: Accessible to Baruch students with ID; located on the ground floor.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Navigate the vertical campus of Baruch College with these ten distinct study environments, from high-tech trading floors to quiet library carrels and outdoor plazas.

cards.title: Engelman Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Newman Library, 2nd Floor
cards.notes: Located on the library's main floor, this designated Whisper Zone offers a silent environment for focused reading and individual work.
cards.short_summary: A strictly silent reading room located on the second floor of the Newman Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Engelman Reading Room is a designated Whisper Zone on the 2nd floor of the Newman Library where no talking is allowed.
cards.source_title: Noise Policy - Baruch College - Newman Library - CUNY
cards.access_notes: Open during library hours; typically 7:00 AM – 11:00 PM on weekdays.

cards.title: Subotnick Financial Services Center
cards.subtitle: Information and Technology Building, 1st Floor
cards.notes: Access professional financial software like Bloomberg and FactSet at 55 workstations in this high-tech trading floor environment.
cards.short_summary: A simulated trading floor providing students with access to professional financial data and software.
cards.evidence_claim: The Subotnick Financial Services Center features the Wasserman Trading Floor with 55 workstations providing access to Bloomberg and FactSet.
cards.source_title: Subotnick Financial Services Center - Zicklin School of Business | Baruch College
cards.access_notes: Open to all Baruch students; valid CUNYCard ID required for entry.

cards.title: Clivner=Field Plaza
cards.subtitle: East 25th Street Pedestrian Plaza
cards.notes: This outdoor pedestrian space features granite seat walls and patterned concrete, ideal for studying between classes in the fresh air.
cards.short_summary: A permanent pedestrian plaza on East 25th Street providing outdoor seating and green space for the campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Clivner=Field Plaza features seating, lighting, and nearly 180 square yards of plantings for student and community use.
cards.source_title: Baruch College Celebrates Official Opening of Clivner=Field Plaza - News Center
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible outdoor space located between Lexington and Third Avenues.

cards.title: Aaronson Student Center
cards.subtitle: East 24th Street (near Lexington Ave)
cards.notes: A dedicated space for undergraduate students to study and congregate, located behind the Madison Square Post Office.
cards.short_summary: An undergraduate-specific student center offering lounge and study space.
cards.evidence_claim: The Allen G. and Mary E. Aaronson Student Center is open for all undergraduate students and is located on East 24th Street.
cards.source_title: Student Center Spaces - Student Affairs | Baruch College
cards.access_notes: Open Monday–Thursday 9:00 AM – 8:00 PM and Friday 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM during semesters.

cards.title: Quiet Study Carrel Rooms
cards.subtitle: Newman Library, Floors 3-5
cards.notes: Check out a key from the 2nd-floor circulation desk to access these individual carrels in locked, quiet rooms.
cards.short_summary: Locked individual study carrels available for daily checkout to ensure a private, quiet workspace.
cards.evidence_claim: Individual study carrels are found in locked rooms on the 3rd-5th floors; keys are checked out from the circulation desk.
cards.source_title: Study Rooms - Baruch College - Newman Library - CUNY
cards.access_notes: First-come, first-served; keys must be returned before the circulation desk closes.

cards.title: NVC Open Study Areas
cards.subtitle: Newman Vertical Campus, Various Floors
cards.notes: Find open seating areas located near the elevator banks on various floors of the 14-story Vertical Campus building.
cards.short_summary: Informal study lounges distributed throughout the floors of the Newman Vertical Campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Open study areas are located on various floors near elevator banks in the Newman Vertical Campus.
cards.source_title: Places To Study on Campus - Student Affairs | Baruch College
cards.access_notes: Available Monday–Friday 7:30 AM – 10:00 PM and weekends 7:30 AM – 5:00 PM.

cards.title: 17 Lex Multi-Purpose Room
cards.subtitle: Field Building, 1st Floor
cards.notes: Equipped with couches, tables, and chairs, this room in the historic 17 Lexington Avenue building serves both undergraduate and graduate students.
cards.short_summary: A versatile study and lounge space located on the first floor of the Lawrence and Eris Field Building.
cards.evidence_claim: The 17 Lex Multi-Purpose Room (MPR) is located at 17 Lexington Avenue on the 1st floor and features couches and tables.
cards.source_title: Student Center Spaces - Student Affairs | Baruch College
cards.access_notes: Open Monday–Thursday 9:30 AM – 7:30 PM and Friday 9:30 AM – 4:30 PM during semesters.

cards.title: Newman Library Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Newman Library, Floors 3-5
cards.notes: Reserve these rooms online for up to two hours for collaborative projects or group exam preparation.
cards.short_summary: Reservable rooms designed for group collaboration and quiet discussion.
cards.evidence_claim: Group study rooms are available on floors 3, 4, and 5 of the Newman Library and can be reserved for 2-hour blocks.
cards.source_title: Study Rooms - Baruch College - Newman Library - CUNY
cards.access_notes: Reservations are held for 15 minutes; room keys are loaned from the 2nd-floor circulation desk.

cards.title: BCTC Student Computing Labs
cards.subtitle: Newman Vertical Campus, 6th Floor
cards.notes: The 6th-floor lab provides extensive computer access and printing services for students needing technical resources.
cards.short_summary: Large-scale computer labs managed by the Baruch Computing & Technology Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The BCTC Student Computing Labs are located on the 6th floor of the Newman Vertical Campus and offer computer access.
cards.source_title: Student Computing Labs - Baruch Computing & Technology Center
cards.access_notes: Typically open 8:00 AM – 10:00 PM on weekdays.

cards.title: Library Study Pods
cards.subtitle: Newman Library, 3rd Floor
cards.notes: These semi-enclosed pods offer a middle ground between open seating and private rooms, suitable for individual focused work.
cards.short_summary: Individual study pods located on the third floor of the Newman Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Newman Library floor plans and study room pages list study pods as available seating on the 3rd floor.
cards.source_title: Floor Plans - Newman Library | Baruch College - CUNY
cards.access_notes: Open seating available to all current CUNY students during library hours.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Use real streets, blocks, corridors, or micro-districts within the practical orbit of this specific campus. Give exactly one sourced reason for each and do not substitute broad city neighborhoods, isolated businesses, safety claims, or demographic stereotypes.

cards.title: The Vertical Campus Corridor
cards.subtitle: Lexington Avenue between 24th and 25th Streets
cards.notes: Walk this block to reach the William and Anita Newman Vertical Campus, the primary hub for Baruch's academic and student life activities.
cards.short_summary: The central corridor for Baruch's main academic building and student services.
cards.evidence_claim: The William and Anita Newman Vertical Campus is located at 55 Lexington Avenue between 24th and 25th Streets.
cards.source_title: Campus Map and Directions - Baruch College
cards.access_notes: Public sidewalk; building access requires a valid CUNY ID card.

cards.title: Clivner=Field Pedestrian Plaza
cards.subtitle: East 25th Street between Lexington and Third Avenues
cards.notes: Gather at this permanent pedestrian plaza for outdoor seating, student events, and a safe walkway between campus buildings.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated pedestrian-only block serving as the college's outdoor student center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Clivner=Field Pedestrian Plaza spans East 25th Street between Lexington and Third Avenues.
cards.source_title: Clivner=Field Plaza - Baruch College
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 to the public as a city-managed pedestrian plaza.

cards.title: The Historic 17 Lex Block
cards.subtitle: Lexington Avenue at East 23rd Street
cards.notes: Visit the Lawrence and Eris Field Building, the historic site of the Free Academy and home to natural science labs.
cards.short_summary: The southern anchor of campus housing the historic Field Building.
cards.evidence_claim: The Lawrence and Eris Field Building is located at 17 Lexington Avenue at the corner of 23rd Street.
cards.source_title: Campus Map and Directions - Baruch College
cards.access_notes: Public street corner; building access requires CUNY ID.

cards.title: Aaronson Student Center Block
cards.subtitle: East 24th Street between Lexington and Third Avenues
cards.notes: Access the Aaronson Student Center, located behind the Madison Square Post Office, for undergraduate lounge space.
cards.short_summary: The block containing the dedicated undergraduate student center entrance.
cards.evidence_claim: The Allen G. and Mary E. Aaronson Student Center entrance is on East 24th Street between Lexington and Third Avenues.
cards.source_title: Student Center Spaces - Baruch College
cards.access_notes: Student center open Monday-Thursday 9am-8pm, Friday 9am-5pm during semesters.

cards.title: The Library & Technology Block
cards.subtitle: East 25th Street between Lexington and Third Avenues
cards.notes: Head to the Information and Technology Building to use the William and Anita Newman Library and computer labs.
cards.short_summary: The block housing the Newman Library and campus technology services.
cards.evidence_claim: The Information and Technology Building (Library Building) is located at 151 East 25th Street.
cards.source_title: Campus Map and Directions - Baruch College
cards.access_notes: Library hours vary; check official site for current late-night study availability.

cards.title: Marxe School Corridor
cards.subtitle: East 22nd Street between Lexington and Third Avenues
cards.notes: Find the Marxe School of Public and International Affairs and the Sidney Mishkin Gallery on this quieter campus block.
cards.short_summary: The southern campus block home to administrative offices and the public policy school.
cards.evidence_claim: The Administrative Building at 135 East 22nd Street houses the Marxe School and the Sidney Mishkin Gallery.
cards.source_title: Campus Map and Directions - Baruch College
cards.access_notes: Public sidewalk; gallery hours are typically Monday-Friday during exhibitions.

cards.title: The Student Dining Strip
cards.subtitle: Third Avenue between 23rd and 25th Streets
cards.notes: Explore various quick-service restaurants and cafes popular with students for lunch breaks between classes.
cards.short_summary: A major commercial avenue adjacent to campus with high-density student dining options.
cards.evidence_claim: Third Avenue is described as an everyday lunch strip for Baruch students due to its proximity to campus buildings.
cards.source_title: Baruch College Guide: Best Restaurants, Bars & Hotels Near Campus (2026)
cards.access_notes: Public commercial street; business hours vary.

cards.title: Madison Square Park Edge
cards.subtitle: Madison Avenue between 23rd and 26th Streets
cards.notes: Walk two blocks west to reach Madison Square Park, a primary green space for students to eat lunch and study outdoors.
cards.short_summary: The western boundary of the campus district bordering a major public park.
cards.evidence_claim: Madison Square Park is a popular lunch spot for Baruch students, located two blocks west of the main campus.
cards.source_title: NYCdata | For Students - Baruch College
cards.access_notes: Public park open daily from 6am to 11pm.

cards.title: The Transit Connection
cards.subtitle: Park Avenue South at East 23rd Street
cards.notes: Use the 23rd Street subway station, recently renamed to include Baruch College, for direct access to the 6 train.
cards.short_summary: The primary subway transit hub for the Baruch College campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The 23rd Street subway station on Park Avenue South officially includes 'Baruch College' in its name as of 2025.
cards.source_title: Baruch College Guide: Best Restaurants, Bars & Hotels Near Campus (2026)
cards.access_notes: Subway station open 24/7; requires MetroCard or OMNY payment.

cards.title: Curry Hill Gateway
cards.subtitle: East 26th Street at Lexington Avenue
cards.notes: Walk one block north of the library to enter Curry Hill, a district known for affordable South Asian dining options.
cards.short_summary: The northern edge of the campus district leading into a famous culinary neighborhood.
cards.evidence_claim: Walking north on Lexington Avenue from Baruch leads into the Curry Hill district within two blocks.
cards.source_title: Baruch College Guide: Best Restaurants, Bars & Hotels Near Campus (2026)
cards.access_notes: Public street; business hours vary.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Discover the unique rituals and annual events that define the Bearcat experience at Baruch College, from historic media milestones to modern campus celebrations.

cards.title: The First-Year Induction
cards.subtitle: Clivner=Field Plaza
cards.notes: Attend the mandatory induction for first-year students followed by a massive club fair on the plaza to kick off the academic year.
cards.short_summary: The official induction ceremony and club fair for incoming first-year students held every August.
cards.evidence_claim: Convocation Day is a mandatory event for first-year students that includes a Club Carnival and campus activities on Clivner=Field Plaza.
cards.source_title: Fall Student Convocation - Baruch College - CUNY
cards.access_notes: Mandatory for first-year students; held annually in late August.

cards.title: The 50-Year Concert Tradition
cards.subtitle: Gramercy Theater
cards.notes: Join the annual concert hosted by WBMB Radio, a tradition spanning five decades that recently moved to the historic Gramercy Theater.
cards.short_summary: An annual live music event hosted by the student radio station WBMB, featuring emerging and established artists.
cards.evidence_claim: WBMB Radio has hosted the annual Spring Fling concert for roughly 50 years, recently moving the event to the Gramercy Theater.
cards.source_title: Spring Fling features Lexa Gates and returning opener Kemmii - The Ticker
cards.access_notes: Held annually in late April or early May; tickets typically required for students.

cards.title: Skating at Rockefeller Center
cards.subtitle: The Rink at Rockefeller Center
cards.notes: Head to Midtown for this annual February tradition where students gather for a night of ice skating at the iconic Rockefeller Center rink.
cards.short_summary: An annual winter event where Baruch students go ice skating together at Rockefeller Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Bearcats on Ice is an annual event hosted at The Rink at Rockefeller Center in February for students to socialize and skate.
cards.source_title: Special Events and Programs - Student Affairs | Baruch College - CUNY
cards.access_notes: Annual February event; requires RSVP through the Office of Student Life.

cards.title: 80 Years of Student Reporting
cards.subtitle: Newman Vertical Campus, Room 3-290
cards.notes: Read the undergraduate newspaper that has been reporting on campus life and city news for over 80 years.
cards.short_summary: The award-winning undergraduate student newspaper of Baruch College, established in 1932.
cards.evidence_claim: The Ticker is the undergraduate student newspaper celebrating over 80 years of reporting news relevant to the Baruch community.
cards.source_title: Student Media at Baruch
cards.access_notes: Published weekly during the academic year; available online and in print across campus.

cards.title: Art in the Business School
cards.subtitle: 135 East 22nd Street
cards.notes: Listen to student-led guides of the college's permanent art collection through the Bloomberg Connects app or during live gallery talks.
cards.short_summary: A tradition of student-led engagement with museum-quality art within a business-focused college environment.
cards.evidence_claim: Mishkin Gallery offers a digital guide where students guide listeners through the Baruch College art collection.
cards.source_title: Mishkin Gallery - Weissman School of Arts and Sciences - CUNY
cards.access_notes: Open to the public during exhibition hours; digital guide available 24/7.

cards.title: The Final Countdown
cards.subtitle: Newman Vertical Campus
cards.notes: Participate in a series of events, giveaways, and professional workshops during the final 100 days of the senior year.
cards.short_summary: A series of celebratory and preparatory events for graduating seniors starting 100 days before commencement.
cards.evidence_claim: 100 Days features a variety of activities including fun events, giveaways, and professional development for graduating students.
cards.source_title: 100 Days - Baruch College Alumni - CUNY
cards.access_notes: Exclusively for graduating seniors; events occur throughout the spring semester.

cards.title: The Lexicon Legacy
cards.subtitle: Newman Vertical Campus
cards.notes: Contribute to or purchase the historic yearbook that has documented Baruch student life since the school's early days.
cards.short_summary: The official yearbook of Baruch College, capturing the history and memories of each graduating class.
cards.evidence_claim: Lexicon is the yearbook of Baruch College, with archives dating back to the school's early history as a business school.
cards.source_title: Yearbook of Baruch College: Lexicon.
cards.access_notes: Yearbooks are produced annually; recent editions have been integrated with The Ticker's operations.

cards.title: LGBTQ+ Achievement Celebration
cards.subtitle: Library Building, Room 750
cards.notes: Attend this annual ceremony that honors the achievements and contributions of LGBTQ+ graduates within the Baruch community.
cards.short_summary: An annual graduation ceremony specifically celebrating LGBTQ+ students and their accomplishments.
cards.evidence_claim: Baruch hosts an annual Lavender Graduation Celebration to honor the success of LGBTQ+ students.
cards.source_title: Class of 2025 Celebrations - Student Affairs | Baruch College - CUNY
cards.access_notes: Held annually in May; open to the Baruch community with RSVP.

cards.title: Honoring the Namesake
cards.subtitle: Campus-wide
cards.notes: Celebrate the legacy of Bernard M. Baruch every August with campus tours and historical retrospectives of his life as a financier.
cards.short_summary: An annual celebration of the birthday and legacy of the college's namesake, Bernard M. Baruch.
cards.evidence_claim: Baruch College celebrates the birthday and legacy of namesake Bernard M. Baruch with tours and historical content.
cards.source_title: Today, Baruch College celebrates the birthday and legacy of our namesake - Facebook
cards.access_notes: Celebrated annually on or around August 19th.

cards.title: The Big Stage Graduation
cards.subtitle: Barclays Center
cards.notes: Cross the stage at the Barclays Center in Brooklyn, a massive venue that hosts the college's large-scale annual commencement ceremony.
cards.short_summary: The annual graduation ceremony for Baruch College, held at the Barclays Center to accommodate the large student body.
cards.evidence_claim: Baruch hosts its annual Commencement ceremony at the Barclays Center in late May or early June.
cards.source_title: Commencement - Student Affairs | Baruch College - CUNY
cards.access_notes: Annual event in late May or early June; tickets required for guests.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at CUNY Bernard M Baruch College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A guide to the essential first-weekend experiences for new Bearcats at Baruch College, focusing on campus traditions and student life hubs.

cards.title: Attend the Official Induction
cards.subtitle: The formal start of your Baruch journey
cards.notes: Join your fellow first-year students for this mandatory ceremonial event to be formally inducted into the college community by campus leaders.
cards.short_summary: The official induction ceremony for all incoming first-year students at Baruch College.
cards.evidence_claim: Fall Student Convocation is a traditional ceremonial event designed to inspire, connect, and induct first year students to the College.
cards.source_title: Fall Student Convocation - Baruch College - CUNY
cards.access_notes: Mandatory for first-year students; typically held on the Thursday before classes begin.

cards.title: Explore the Club Carnival
cards.subtitle: Student life on the 25th Street Plaza
cards.notes: Head to the pedestrian plaza after Convocation to meet student organization leaders and find your community at the annual Club Carnival.
cards.short_summary: The central outdoor hub for student activities and the annual Club Carnival event.
cards.evidence_claim: The celebration continues throughout the day with additional events as part of Weeks of Welcome... Visit the Club Carnival... Location: Clivner=Field Plaza.
cards.source_title: Fall Student Convocation - Baruch College - CUNY
cards.access_notes: Open public pedestrian space located on East 25th Street between Lexington and Third Avenues.

cards.title: Shoot Hoops in the Main Gym
cards.subtitle: Open play at the Vertical Campus
cards.notes: Visit the basement levels of the NVC for open play in the Main Gym to meet other students through sports during the first weekend.
cards.short_summary: The multi-level athletic facility located beneath the Newman Vertical Campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Enjoy open play in the Main Gym... Location: Clivner=Field Plaza [entrance nearby]. The ARC occupies the three basement levels within the Vertical Campus.
cards.source_title: Membership Information - Baruch College Athletics - CUNY
cards.access_notes: Access requires a valid Baruch student ID; hours vary by semester and are reduced on weekends.

cards.title: Find Your Favorite Study Nook
cards.subtitle: Quiet floors for weekend prep
cards.notes: Scout out a quiet spot in the library early; it's a key resource for managing the rigorous Baruch academic workload from day one.
cards.short_summary: The primary academic library for Baruch College, offering extensive study spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The main library is open from 7am-midnight everyday. [Note: Current hours may vary, check official site].
cards.source_title: Hours - Newman Library | Baruch College - CUNY
cards.access_notes: Located at 151 East 25th Street. Valid Baruch ID required for entry.

cards.title: View the Latest Exhibition
cards.subtitle: Art and culture on 22nd Street
cards.notes: Take a break from the bustle of the Vertical Campus to explore contemporary art exhibitions at the college's dedicated gallery space.
cards.short_summary: Baruch's professional art gallery featuring rotating exhibitions and the college's permanent collection.
cards.evidence_claim: All Mishkin Gallery programs are free and open to the public... 135 East 22nd Street, New York, NY 10010.
cards.source_title: Mishkin Gallery - Weissman School of Arts and Sciences - CUNY
cards.access_notes: Open to the public; check website for current exhibition dates and seasonal closures.

cards.title: Grab Lunch at the NVC
cards.subtitle: The social heart of the building
cards.notes: The first-floor cafeteria is the primary meeting spot for students between classes and a great place to connect during the first weekend.
cards.short_summary: The main dining and social area located on the first floor of the Newman Vertical Campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Newman Vertical Campus 1st Floor Cafeteria Mon.-Fri. 7:30am-10:00pm. Sat.-Sun. 7:30am-5:00pm.
cards.source_title: Places To Study on Campus - Student Affairs | Baruch College
cards.access_notes: Located on the 1st floor of the NVC at 55 Lexington Avenue.

cards.title: Relax in the Student Lounge
cards.subtitle: A dedicated space for undergraduates
cards.notes: Visit the Aaronson Student Center to relax between orientation sessions or meet up with your new First Year Seminar cohort.
cards.short_summary: A modern lounge and meeting space specifically for Baruch undergraduate students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Allen G. and Mary E. Aaronson Student Center (ASC) is open for all undergraduate students.
cards.source_title: Student Center Spaces - Baruch College
cards.access_notes: Entrance on East 24th Street between Lexington and Third Avenues. Closed on weekends.

cards.title: Pick Up Your Bearcat Gear
cards.subtitle: Stock up on essentials
cards.notes: Visit the bookstore to get your textbooks and some Baruch apparel to show your school spirit during the first week of classes.
cards.short_summary: The official campus bookstore for textbooks, supplies, and Baruch-branded merchandise.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bearcat Bookstore is listed as a key resource for students on the official events calendar.
cards.source_title: Upcoming Events: Baruch College Events Calendar
cards.access_notes: Located at 55 Lexington Avenue (Newman Vertical Campus).

cards.title: Challenge a Peer to a Game
cards.subtitle: Fun and games in the NVC
cards.notes: Stop by the Game Room in the Newman Vertical Campus for a quick round of pool or table tennis to unwind after a day of orientation.
cards.short_summary: A recreational space managed by the Office of Student Life for student leisure.
cards.evidence_claim: Game Room Fall/Spring Hours: Monday–Thursday: 10:00 a.m.–7:30 p.m. Friday: 10:00 a.m.–4:30 p.m. Closed on weekends.
cards.source_title: About the Office of Student Life - Baruch College
cards.access_notes: Located in Room 2-210 of the Newman Vertical Campus.

cards.title: Join the Weeks of Welcome
cards.subtitle: A series of kickoff events
cards.notes: Participate in the various WoW events, from open houses to social mixers, designed to help you navigate campus and meet fellow Bearcats.
cards.short_summary: A multi-week series of programs and events to welcome new and returning students each semester.
cards.evidence_claim: Weeks of Welcome (WoW) is a dynamic series of events designed to help you feel at home, meet fellow Bearcats, and explore everything our vibrant campus has to offer.
cards.source_title: Weeks of Welcome 2026! - Baruch College - CUNY
cards.access_notes: Events take place across various campus locations during the first two weeks of the semester.
